title: Modernism in the Arts
summary: Modernism names the run of art movements from Courbet's realism to abstract art and its developments in the 1960s, at its most prominent between the world wars. Modernists rejected realistic depiction for experiment with form, shape, colour and line, tending towards abstraction and stressing materials and process, often with utopian social aims. Modernist architects and designers took the machine as their model, rejected ornament, and used steel, concrete and glass to build cheaply for the masses; form followed function. Postmodernism arose as a reaction against it.

uncertainty.note: Modernism developed across several decades, rooted in late 19th-century movements and continuing until the emergence of postmodernism in the 1960s.
